name: The Lime of Macharen Church
age_estimate: roughly 190 years, from a registered planting decade
access: Free. Village square (plein) owned by the municipality; register: visitable ja, visible ja, openbaar ja. No hours; open at all times.
transport: No railway station in Macharen; bus from Oss, not verified here (check the current timetable). About 8 km by road from Oss station.
story:
A lime planted in the 1830s stands in the middle of a road junction in Macharen, inside a raised, heart-shaped tree pit. The Sint-Petrus-Bandenkerk stands behind it.

The national register of monumental trees puts its planting in the decade 1830 to 1840, which makes it somewhere between 186 and 196 years old. It is the 'Pallida' form of the common lime, 3.5 metres round and 17 metres tall by the register's figures, which carry no measurement date.

Nobody wrote down why it was planted, or by whom. The register's history field says simply 'unknown', and the church behind it is no evidence either way. What the register does record is a tree that has been looked after. An inspector in January 1994 found a lot of dead wood and asked for it to be cleared and for the ground around the roots to be studied. At the 2023 visit the tree stood in its raised tub on a bed of wood chips, still listed as monumental.

It was not the only registered lime in the village. A second one, at the primary school De Linde on Hoogstraat, is recorded as dead, so this is the one to come for.

Macharen is a village in the municipality of Oss, about eight kilometres from the town. If you know why this lime was planted, tell us.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the raised, heart-shaped tree pit it grows from, in the middle of the junction. It stands in front of the Sint-Petrus-Bandenkerk at Dorpstraat 1.

best_time.label: late June into July, when the cream flowers open and the scent carries across the junction

name: The Lulboom of Megen
age_estimate: roughly 90 years, from a documented planting in 1937

location.address: Megen, Maasdijk, nabij afrit naar 't Veer

access: Free. Public planting (plantsoen) on the Maasdijk owned by the municipality, with a bench beside it; register: visitable ja, visible ja, openbaar ja. No hours; open at all times.
transport: No railway station in Megen; bus from Oss, not verified here (check the current timetable). About 14 km by road from Oss station.
story:
Two cannons dated 1809 and 1811 stand under this lime, more than a century older than the tree that shades them. The tree itself is the Lulboom of Megen, and its name translates, politely, as the chatter tree: in Dutch, lullen is to talk at length about not very much. The register's history notes say it became a meeting place for young and old, with a bench beside it looking out from the Maasdijk, and that is where the name comes from.

It went in with more ceremony than its nickname suggests. The silver lime was planted as a memorial tree for the wedding of Princess Juliana and Prince Bernhard in 1937, placed as a royal lime at a prominent spot just outside the historic core of Megen. That makes it about 90 years old, young for this map, but in that time it has put on 3.9 metres of girth and 17 metres of height, by the register's undated figures.

Its worst day is on record. A storm on Ascension Day 1992 split and damaged the tree, and the Heidemij braced and anchored it the same year. It was last inspected in 2023 and is still listed as monumental. Since at least 2023 the spot has also hosted Lulboompop, a music festival held at the tree every June.

All of this rests on one source, the national register of monumental trees, which entered the lime twice and later withdrew the duplicate. Megen lies 14 kilometres from Oss.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the two cannons, dated 1809 and 1811, standing under its crown. It stands alone on the grass triangle between the Maasdijk path and the road down to 't Veer, with a bench beside it.

best_time.label: July, when it flowers after the other limes, strongly scented of honey

name: The Silver Maple of Gripper
age_estimate: roughly 130 years, from a registered planting decade
verified_sources: https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse?format=jsonv2&lat=51.76683&lon=5.5311&zoom=18 (OpenStreetMap: the point lies on a leisure=playground way on the street Gripper)
access: Free. Municipal planting (plantsoen) at the playground on the residential street Gripper, central Oss; register: visitable ja, visible ja, openbaar ja. OpenStreetMap maps the spot as a playground. No hours; open at all times.
transport: Oss station is roughly 0.7 km west, about a 10 minute walk through the town centre.
story:
For years nobody could measure this tree, because nobody could get to it. When the national register of monumental trees noted the silver maple, it stood inside a closed factory yard in the centre of Oss, and the entry said a girth measurement was impossible and that building plans were being prepared.

The plans happened, and the tree stayed. The factory site became housing, the address changed in December 2017 from Bram van de Berghstraat 22 to Gripper 28, and the maple now stands in a municipal planting by a playground, between the brick-paved street and the new houses. A register photograph from 2023 shows it in its new setting, and an inspector saw it again in March 2026.

The register now gives it a girth of 4.31 metres and a height of 20 metres. It does not say when that girth was taken, so read it as the register's figure rather than a fresh measurement, though it is a believable size for a silver maple of this age. The planting is put in the 1890s, which makes it roughly 126 to 136 years old: a North American species that has spent its whole life in the middle of a Brabant town.

What it saw inside those walls, the register does not say; its history field reads 'unknown'. If you know who planted it, or what the factory made, tell us.

It is a ten-minute walk from Oss station.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the one big crown between the brick-paved street and the new houses, 20 metres tall on a trunk 4.31 metres round. It stands beside the playground at Gripper 28 to 30.
